summary: Session 2 of 4: one authored scenario now renders four documents that cannot drift apart. ai_router/scenario.py is the platform-neutral model -- stable kebab-case scenario and step ids, prerequisites, a baseline carrying its own observable, reset, recovery, named checkpoints, and per step an action plus the expected observable result -- with closed vocabularies at both levels, so an unknown key, a duplicate key and a '-->' that would break a WebVTT cue are all refused rather than silently absorbed. ai_router/scenario_render.py renders walkthrough.md, training.md, captions.vtt and chapters.json, and its --check re-renders in memory and refuses any committed file whose text differs; the pytest suite runs that over the whole committed tree, which is the divergence gate the session owed. THE DRIVER QUARANTINE IS STRUCTURAL, not conventional: render_all hands each renderer a copy with drivers emptied, and portable_digest never sees driver blocks, so replacing the entire driver block leaves all four documents identical -- asserted, including a stub renderer that proves it is handed {}. ai_router/scenario_lint.py is the advisory second line for selector-shaped text that leaks into portable prose; six rules, each with a planted violation and a legitimate look-alike, and the committed corpus asserted clean. The operator's 2026-08-10 condition on cutting the synced window is honoured in what the documents SAY: both state, verbatim, that reaching any step means replaying a prefix from the baseline or the nearest named checkpoint, and walkthrough.md renders a Where to start table instead of implying a seek bar. Both prose documents also state verbatim that no video is needed and link no media file. One exemplar ships: docs/walkthroughs/work-explorer-first-look, five steps reading the AI Work Explorer on the disposable fixture project npm run walk stages, with every expected result checked against shipped extension code and the pinned uat-matrix fixtures. Verification ran four rounds and found three Majors -- two of them the same defect seen independently by two lenses -- plus eight nits. The Major that mattered: the exemplar declared its audience as anyone who had installed the extension while its baseline needed a repository checkout and an unstated starting directory, so the first command failed before step 1 in a document whose entire claim is that a stranger can follow it. The second Major, found by the supplementary pass, was that the quarantine lint had no CSS id rule at all; the first fix for it was then REJECTED on the fix delta for missing button#save, which is the form browser tooling emits and which survives an unquoted YAML scalar. Both are fixed and the verifier's own executable acceptance criterion was run verbatim. One nit was disputed with deterministic evidence rather than accepted: comparing raw bytes instead of text would fail --check on every Windows clone of this repo (core.autocrlf=true; .gitattributes exempts only the stamped verification artifacts), so the wrong thing was the byte-for-byte CLAIM, which is corrected everywhere, with two tests pinning that the tolerance is line endings and nothing more. Two Minor residuals ship unfixed and named (S2-R1, S2-R2), both found by the final VERIFIED round: neither could be fixed without a delta-scoped remediation-review past the 2-cycle cap, which the orchestrator may not self-authorize, and shipping a named residual beats shipping unverified code.
